meta.title: FARM127 Charlotte Young Adult Resource Navigator
meta.description: A working directory of reputable Charlotte/Mecklenburg, North Carolina and national resources that can serve young adults.

resources.name: NC 211
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult has multiple needs and FARM127 is unsure where to start.
resources.eligibility: Anyone in North Carolina.
resources.provides: Free, confidential, multilingual navigation to food, housing, health, transportation, legal and other community resources.
resources.access: Call 2-1-1, call 888-892-1162, or search the online database.
resources.caveat: Directory information changes; confirm the referred provider's current intake requirements.

resources.name: Mecklenburg County Community Resource Centers
resources.referralTrigger: Help applying for county benefits or connecting to multiple county services.
resources.eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents; program-specific eligibility applies.
resources.provides: In-person access to benefit applications, case navigation and partner services.
resources.access: Visit a Community Resource Center or use Mecklenburg County's contact options.
resources.location: Ella B. Scarborough CRC, 430 Stitt Rd; Valerie C. Woodard CRC, 3205 Freedom Dr.
resources.caveat: Services and walk-in hours vary by site.

resources.name: City of Charlotte Community Resources Directory
resources.referralTrigger: Finding additional local providers by need area.
resources.eligibility: Charlotte-area residents; eligibility varies by listed provider.
resources.provides: City-maintained directory of community organizations and services.
resources.access: Search the online directory, then verify eligibility directly with the provider.
resources.caveat: A directory is a starting point, not a guarantee of availability.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Coordinated Entry
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult is homeless, sleeping somewhere unsafe, or likely to lose housing soon.
resources.eligibility: Individuals and families who are homeless or at risk in Mecklenburg County.
resources.provides: Community entry process for shelter, diversion, rapid rehousing and supportive housing resources.
resources.access: Call and complete a telephone assessment; follow instructions for an in-person assessment when requested.
resources.caveat: Housing is not immediate or guaranteed; callbacks may take up to two business days and programs have limited capacity.

resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
resources.referralTrigger: Suicidal thoughts, mental-health crisis, severe emotional distress or concern about another person.
resources.eligibility: Anyone in the United States.
resources.provides: 24/7 call, text and chat crisis support and connection to local crisis services.
resources.access: Call or text 988. Call 911 for an immediate life-threatening emergency.
resources.location: Nationwide; routes to local crisis support.
resources.caveat: Not a replacement for emergency medical response when there is immediate danger.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Mobile Crisis (Santé Group)
resources.referralTrigger: A behavioral-health crisis may be managed safely in the community rather than through law enforcement or an emergency department.
resources.eligibility: People in Mecklenburg County experiencing a mental-health or substance-use crisis.
resources.provides: 24/7 crisis assessment, de-escalation and connection to treatment.
resources.access: Call the local mobile crisis line and select option 1.
resources.caveat: Response depends on safety, staffing and clinical assessment; call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: Alliance Health Access and Information Line
resources.referralTrigger: Finding publicly funded mental-health, substance-use or developmental-disability services.
resources.eligibility: Alliance Health service-area residents; funding and clinical eligibility vary.
resources.provides: 24/7 behavioral-health information, screening and provider connection.
resources.access: Call the access and information line.
resources.location: Mecklenburg County and Alliance Health service area.
resources.caveat: Provider openings and funding authorization vary.

resources.name: 911 Emergency Services
resources.referralTrigger: Immediate danger, violence, overdose, serious injury, fire or a life-threatening medical emergency.
resources.eligibility: Anyone in an emergency.
resources.provides: Police, fire and emergency medical response.
resources.access: Call 911 and give the location, nature of the emergency and immediate safety concerns.
resources.caveat: Use crisis or non-emergency resources when there is no immediate threat to life or safety.

resources.name: Mecklenburg County LINKS
resources.referralTrigger: A current or former foster youth needs independent-living planning, funding or case coordination.
resources.eligibility: Generally youth ages 13–21 who are or were in foster care; specific services depend on custody/status.
resources.provides: Independent-living assessment, planning, education, housing and other transition assistance.
resources.access: Contact Mecklenburg Youth and Family Services / LINKS.
resources.caveat: Age and custody rules are strict; refer before age 21 whenever possible.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Phoenix Project
resources.referralTrigger: A former foster youth under 21 who is no longer in county custody needs transition support.
resources.eligibility: Young adults generally under age 21 who left foster care; confirm individual eligibility.
resources.provides: Post-custody independent-living support, case coordination and access to eligible funds/services.
resources.access: Call the Phoenix Project office and request an eligibility review.
resources.caveat: Do not wait until close to the 21st birthday; funding and services are eligibility-dependent.

resources.name: NC Foster Care 18 to 21 / Voluntary Placement Agreement
resources.referralTrigger: A youth is approaching age 18 in foster care and needs continued placement, case management or financial support.
resources.eligibility: Youth who meet North Carolina's criteria and enter a voluntary agreement; generally available until age 21.
resources.provides: Continued foster-care placement, case management, resources and financial assistance while pursuing an approved path.
resources.access: Ask the county social worker before discharge from care; review the state eligibility rules.
resources.location: North Carolina; administered through county child welfare.
resources.caveat: Timing matters. Leaving care without completing the agreement can make access harder.

resources.name: Mecklenburg GEAR Up Supplemental Income Pilot
resources.referralTrigger: An eligible young adult aging out needs flexible monthly cash support for rent, food, transportation or other stability needs.
resources.eligibility: Pilot announced for certain Mecklenburg young adults ages 18–21 aging out of foster care.
resources.provides: Monthly supplemental income plus support coordination.
resources.access: Call Mecklenburg LINKS at 704-336-KIDS and ask whether the pilot is still enrolling or accepting referrals.
resources.caveat: Pilot status, enrollment slots and funding beyond the announced cohort were not confirmed for August 2026.

resources.name: NC Medicaid for Former Foster Care Youth
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult who aged out of foster care needs health coverage.
resources.eligibility: Certain young adults under age 26 who were in foster care and enrolled in Medicaid when they aged out; rules depend on foster-care state and history.
resources.provides: Medicaid medical and behavioral-health coverage.
resources.access: Apply through ePASS or Mecklenburg County and explicitly identify former foster-care status.
resources.caveat: Eligibility details changed under federal/state policy; obtain a formal Medicaid determination rather than assuming eligibility.

resources.name: NC Medicaid Children and Families Specialty Plan
resources.referralTrigger: A Medicaid-enrolled young adult with current or former child-welfare involvement needs coordinated physical, behavioral and social care.
resources.eligibility: Eligible Medicaid beneficiaries involved with the child-welfare system, including certain former foster youth under 26.
resources.provides: Specialized Medicaid health plan with care management and trauma-informed provider coordination.
resources.access: Confirm enrollment through NC Medicaid / the specialty plan and update contact information.
resources.caveat: Enrollment is eligibility-based; not every former foster youth will be automatically assigned.

resources.name: NC Reach
resources.referralTrigger: Paying tuition and school costs at a North Carolina public college or university.
resources.eligibility: Eligible NC residents who aged out of foster care at 18 or were adopted from foster care after age 12; must attend at least half time at an eligible NC public institution.
resources.provides: State-funded last-dollar scholarship and student support.
resources.access: Complete FAFSA and apply through NC Reach / CFNC.
resources.location: North Carolina public community colleges and universities.
resources.caveat: Deadlines and satisfactory academic progress apply; begin before enrollment.

resources.name: Education and Training Voucher (ETV)
resources.referralTrigger: Paying education, training, housing, books or other approved postsecondary costs.
resources.eligibility: Eligible current/former foster youth and some youth adopted or placed in guardianship; age and status rules apply.
resources.provides: Federal voucher funding of up to the program limit for eligible postsecondary expenses.
resources.access: Apply through the Foster Care to Success ETV portal and coordinate with LINKS/financial aid.
resources.caveat: Awards depend on eligibility, annual funding, enrollment and documentation; do not assume the full maximum.

resources.name: Youth Villages LifeSet
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult leaving foster care needs intensive, relationship-based help with housing, work, education, health and daily living.
resources.eligibility: Generally ages 17.5–23 leaving foster care; local referral and program criteria apply.
resources.provides: Community-based specialist support focused on stable housing, employment, education, relationships and well-being.
resources.access: Contact Youth Villages North Carolina and request a LifeSet referral assessment.
resources.caveat: Capacity and referral-source requirements vary; verify local Charlotte openings.

resources.name: The Relatives — On Ramp Resource Center
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult ages 16–24 needs one place for broad youth-centered case management and resource connection.
resources.eligibility: Young people ages 16–24 in Mecklenburg County; foster-care history is not required.
resources.provides: Case management, employment, education, housing navigation, basic needs and connections to partner services.
resources.access: Walk in or call the resource center.
resources.caveat: Hours and same-day service capacity can change; call before traveling.

resources.name: The Relatives — Young Adult Housing
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult ages 18–24 is homeless, at risk of homelessness or fleeing domestic violence.
resources.eligibility: Young adults ages 18–24 meeting the program's housing-risk criteria.
resources.provides: Scattered-site housing plus case management and support toward long-term stability.
resources.access: Contact The Relatives and ask for young-adult housing screening.
resources.caveat: Units and subsidies are limited; eligibility does not guarantee immediate placement.

resources.name: Charlotte Angels — Dare to Dream
resources.referralTrigger: A youth or young adult in foster care needs a consistent mentor and relational support.
resources.eligibility: Youth and young adults in foster care, generally ages 11–22; matching criteria apply.
resources.provides: Long-term volunteer mentoring, goal support and relational consistency.
resources.access: Submit a youth/mentor inquiry through Charlotte Angels.
resources.caveat: Mentor matching depends on volunteer availability and safety-screening processes.

resources.name: SaySo / Strong Able Youth Speaking Out
resources.referralTrigger: A current or former foster youth wants peer connection, leadership, advocacy and transition information.
resources.eligibility: Young people with out-of-home-care experience; published age ranges vary by activity, generally teens through mid-20s.
resources.provides: Youth-led peer network, conferences, advocacy, leadership and transition resources.
resources.access: Join through SaySo or Children's Home Society of North Carolina.
resources.caveat: Confirm the age range and event eligibility for the specific activity.

resources.name: HUD Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) Voucher
resources.referralTrigger: A former foster youth ages 18–24 is homeless or at risk and needs a time-limited housing voucher.
resources.eligibility: Federal criteria generally include leaving foster care, ages 18–24 and homelessness/housing instability; local referral partnership is required.
resources.provides: Housing Choice Voucher assistance with supportive services for eligible former foster youth.
resources.access: Ask Mecklenburg LINKS and INLIVIAN whether an active FYI referral pathway currently exists.
resources.caveat: Federal availability does not prove local voucher availability. Treat this as a referral-pathway lead until INLIVIAN confirms.

resources.name: I Am Here Vital Document Legal Hotline
resources.referralTrigger: A young person experiencing homelessness lacks a birth certificate, state ID or other vital document.
resources.eligibility: Young people experiencing homelessness; case eligibility is assessed by the hotline.
resources.provides: Free legal help obtaining identification and vital documents.
resources.access: Call or text the hotline and leave a message if unanswered.
resources.caveat: Published hotline hours have varied; confirm the current schedule and expect callback-based service.

resources.name: National Runaway Safeline
resources.referralTrigger: A young person is away from home, considering leaving, unsafe, disconnected from family or needs help returning safely.
resources.eligibility: Youth and young adults; Home Free transportation generally serves ages 12–21.
resources.provides: 24/7 confidential crisis support, mediated communication, local referrals and eligible transportation home.
resources.access: Call 1-800-RUNAWAY, text or use online chat.
resources.caveat: Not a local housing program; transportation and reunification services have specific criteria.

resources.name: Roof Above — Day Services Center
resources.referralTrigger: An unstably housed or homeless adult needs meals, showers, laundry, mail, charging, basic medical help or a housing entry point.
resources.eligibility: Adults experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
resources.provides: Lunch, showers, laundry, restrooms, mail, device charging, ID assistance, limited bus passes and connections to shelter/housing.
resources.access: Visit the Day Services Center; call Coordinated Entry first for housing/shelter assessment.
resources.caveat: Hours and individual services vary; some assistance requires verification or sign-up.

resources.name: Roof Above — Men's Emergency Shelter
resources.referralTrigger: An unaccompanied adult who identifies as male needs emergency shelter.
resources.eligibility: Age 18+, unaccompanied and identifies as male.
resources.provides: Year-round shelter beds, meals, showers, laundry, employment and housing-navigation support.
resources.access: Complete Coordinated Entry and follow the shelter lottery/enrollment instructions.
resources.location: Tryon Shelter, 1210 N. Tryon St.; Howard Levine Men's Shelter, 3406 Statesville Ave.
resources.caveat: Beds are limited and may use a lottery; overnight overflow procedures differ.

resources.name: The Salvation Army Center of Hope
resources.referralTrigger: A woman, with or without children, needs emergency shelter.
resources.eligibility: Women and children experiencing homelessness; intake and safety criteria apply.
resources.provides: Emergency shelter, food, basic needs and connections to supportive services.
resources.access: Call Coordinated Entry or the Center of Hope intake line.
resources.caveat: Bed availability is limited; call before arrival.

resources.name: Crisis Assistance Ministry — Emergency Financial Assistance
resources.referralTrigger: A Mecklenburg household is behind on rent or utilities or faces a short-term financial crisis.
resources.eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents who meet documentation and program requirements.
resources.provides: Emergency rent and utility assistance plus financial coaching.
resources.access: Review required documents and apply through the Get Help process.
resources.caveat: Funding is limited and changes frequently; assistance is not guaranteed and may not cover all arrears.

resources.name: Crisis Assistance Ministry — Free Store
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs clothing, shoes, linens or essential household goods at no cost.
resources.eligibility: People meeting the Free Store's current service requirements.
resources.provides: Free donated clothing, shoes and household items.
resources.access: Check the current Free Store process and visit during service hours.
resources.caveat: Inventory varies; specific sizes or items are not guaranteed.

resources.name: INLIVIAN — Housing Choice Voucher and Public Housing
resources.referralTrigger: A very-low-income young adult needs long-term subsidized housing.
resources.eligibility: Income, household and program rules apply; waitlist selection is required.
resources.provides: Public housing and Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance.
resources.access: Check the current waitlist status and apply only through official INLIVIAN channels.
resources.caveat: Waitlists are often closed or open only for limited periods; never pay a third party to apply.

resources.name: Charlotte Family Housing
resources.referralTrigger: A family with a minor child is homeless or unstably housed and needs temporary housing plus intensive support.
resources.eligibility: Families with at least one minor child; program screening applies.
resources.provides: Temporary housing, case management, employment/financial support and transition to permanent housing.
resources.access: Contact the organization and complete its intake/referral process.
resources.caveat: Not for unaccompanied adults without children; capacity is limited.

resources.name: YWCA Central Carolinas — Transitional Housing
resources.referralTrigger: A single woman or a family with children needs transitional housing and case management.
resources.eligibility: Women in Transition serves single women; Families Together serves families with minor children; screening applies.
resources.provides: Furnished transitional housing, case management and stability planning.
resources.access: Review the relevant housing program and request intake.
resources.caveat: Program fit and openings vary; this is not same-day emergency shelter.

resources.name: Time Out Youth — Housing & Supportive Services
resources.referralTrigger: An LGBTQ+ young adult needs affirming housing navigation, case management or basic needs.
resources.eligibility: LGBTQ+ young adults, generally ages 18–24 for housing services; specific service ages vary.
resources.provides: Housing case management, document/benefit help, food, showers, laundry, clothing, education and employment support.
resources.access: Contact Time Out Youth and request housing/supportive-services intake.
resources.caveat: Housing resources are limited and eligibility differs by program.

resources.name: Safe Alliance — Domestic Violence Shelter
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult is fleeing intimate-partner violence or needs a confidential safety plan and shelter.
resources.eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence; adults and children; safety screening applies.
resources.provides: 24/7 hotline, emergency shelter, safety planning, counseling and victim support.
resources.access: Call the Greater Charlotte Hope Line.
resources.location: Charlotte / Mecklenburg County; shelter location is confidential.
resources.caveat: Use 911 for immediate danger. Shelter placement depends on safety and capacity.

resources.name: Gracious Hands Transitional Housing
resources.referralTrigger: A woman experiencing or nearing homelessness needs transitional housing and life-skills support.
resources.eligibility: Women meeting program intake criteria; confirm whether children can be accommodated.
resources.provides: Transitional housing, case management and life-skills support.
resources.access: Contact the organization for a current eligibility and vacancy screening.
resources.caveat: Program size and openings are limited; verify current admission criteria directly.

resources.name: Crittenton of North Carolina
resources.referralTrigger: A pregnant or parenting young woman needs residential support, safety, education or family-stability services.
resources.eligibility: Women and families meeting the criteria for a specific Crittenton program.
resources.provides: Residential and community programs supporting health, parenting, education and self-sufficiency.
resources.access: Call and request screening for the appropriate program.
resources.caveat: Programs have distinct eligibility; not all services are available to every applicant.

resources.name: MiraVia College Residence
resources.referralTrigger: A pregnant college student or new mother needs free residential support while continuing school.
resources.eligibility: Generally age 18+, pregnant or parenting a newborn, enrolled in college and meeting program screening requirements.
resources.provides: Free residential community, meals/support and help continuing postsecondary education.
resources.access: Review eligibility and contact MiraVia for an application.
resources.caveat: Narrow eligibility and limited residential capacity.

resources.name: Community Link
resources.referralTrigger: A low- or moderate-income worker needs help obtaining or keeping safe, affordable housing or improving financial readiness.
resources.eligibility: Program-specific income and housing criteria apply.
resources.provides: Housing counseling, financial literacy, homelessness services, homeownership education and referrals.
resources.access: Contact Community Link and request the appropriate counseling or housing service.
resources.caveat: Some programs focus on working households or homeownership rather than immediate shelter.

resources.name: Roof Above — Rapid Rehousing & Permanent Supportive Housing
resources.referralTrigger: A person experiencing homelessness needs rental subsidy, housing navigation or long-term supportive housing.
resources.eligibility: Rapid rehousing and supportive-housing programs have different federal homelessness and vulnerability criteria.
resources.provides: Housing identification, move-in/rent assistance, case management and permanent supportive housing.
resources.access: Enter through Mecklenburg Coordinated Entry.
resources.caveat: A referral from Coordinated Entry is required; long waits and documentation requirements are common.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Targeted Housing Assistance Program (THAP-IN)
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult ages 18–24 is at imminent risk of homelessness and flexible cash support could prevent housing loss.
resources.eligibility: Pilot criteria have included Mecklenburg young adults ages 18–24 at imminent risk; current enrollment must be confirmed.
resources.provides: Flexible cash assistance paired with navigation/coaching.
resources.access: Ask The Relatives, Coordinated Entry or the local Continuum of Care whether the pilot is currently accepting referrals.
resources.caveat: Pilot funding and intake status were not confirmed for August 2026.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP/FNS)
resources.referralTrigger: A low-income young adult needs recurring grocery assistance.
resources.eligibility: Income, household and immigration/status rules apply.
resources.provides: Electronic benefits for purchasing eligible food.
resources.access: Apply through ePASS, a Community Resource Center or Mecklenburg County.
resources.caveat: Processing and verification take time; expedited benefits are available only when statutory criteria are met.

resources.name: Nourish Up — Food Share and Meals
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult or household needs pantry groceries or prepared meal support.
resources.eligibility: Charlotte/Mecklenburg residents; distribution requirements vary by program/site.
resources.provides: Food pantries, grocery distribution and meal delivery through local partners.
resources.access: Use the Food Share access process or call for the closest distribution option.
resources.caveat: Sites, appointment rules and food availability vary.

resources.name: Second Harvest Food Bank of Metrolina
resources.referralTrigger: Finding an emergency food pantry or getting help applying for SNAP.
resources.eligibility: Residents in the regional service area; partner pantry rules vary.
resources.provides: Food locator, partner pantry network and SNAP application assistance.
resources.access: Use the Need Food locator; contact a listed partner before traveling.
resources.caveat: The warehouse generally is not a public walk-in pantry; service is delivered through partners.

resources.name: Mecklenburg WIC
resources.referralTrigger: A pregnant person, new parent or caregiver of a child under five needs nutrition support.
resources.eligibility: Pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding people and children under five who meet income/nutrition criteria.
resources.provides: Healthy-food benefits, nutrition education, breastfeeding support and health referrals.
resources.access: Call Mecklenburg Public Health to apply or schedule an appointment.
resources.caveat: Not available to young adults without pregnancy/young-child eligibility.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Department of Community Resources — Apply for Benefits
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult may qualify for Medicaid, SNAP, Work First, energy or other public benefits.
resources.eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents; each benefit has separate eligibility.
resources.provides: Application intake and case processing for major county-administered benefits.
resources.access: Apply online through ePASS or contact Mecklenburg County.
resources.caveat: One application does not guarantee eligibility; submit requested documents promptly.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Energy Assistance (LIEAP/CIP)
resources.referralTrigger: A low-income household is struggling with heating/cooling bills or faces an energy crisis.
resources.eligibility: Income and program-specific household criteria apply.
resources.provides: Seasonal energy assistance and crisis intervention payments.
resources.access: Apply through Mecklenburg County during the applicable program period.
resources.caveat: Funding is seasonal and finite; application windows and priority groups change.

resources.name: Work First Family Assistance (TANF)
resources.referralTrigger: A very-low-income young adult is caring for a child and needs cash assistance plus employment services.
resources.eligibility: Low-income families with children; work and program participation rules apply.
resources.provides: Time-limited cash assistance, employment services and supportive benefits.
resources.access: Apply through Mecklenburg Department of Community Resources.
resources.caveat: Generally not available to childless adults; sanctions and time limits apply.

resources.name: Common Wealth Charlotte
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs budgeting, credit repair, banking access, debt planning or a safe small-dollar loan option.
resources.eligibility: Charlotte-area residents; specific products/services have eligibility rules.
resources.provides: Free financial counseling, workshops, safe banking access, credit guidance and eligible 0% loans after counseling.
resources.access: Call or schedule a financial counseling session.
resources.caveat: Loans are not automatic; participation and underwriting criteria apply.

resources.name: Child Care Resources Inc. — Child Care Subsidy Support
resources.referralTrigger: A parenting young adult needs affordable child care to work, attend school or training.
resources.eligibility: Families meeting income, activity and child-age criteria; waitlists may apply.
resources.provides: Help understanding and applying for child-care subsidy plus child-care search support.
resources.access: Call the subsidy information line or use the website.
resources.caveat: Subsidy funding and waitlists fluctuate; child-care placement is separate from subsidy approval.

resources.name: Social Security — SSI / SSDI
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult has a documented disability that substantially limits work and may qualify for federal income support.
resources.eligibility: Federal disability, work-credit and financial criteria apply.
resources.provides: Monthly disability income and potential connection to health coverage.
resources.access: Apply through the Social Security Administration; gather medical and work documentation.
resources.caveat: Applications are evidence-heavy and often denied initially; legal assistance may be useful for appeals.

resources.name: Teen Health Connection
resources.referralTrigger: A young person needs adolescent/young-adult primary care, behavioral health, nutrition or health education in one setting.
resources.eligibility: Generally ages 11–25.
resources.provides: Integrated medical and behavioral-health care tailored to adolescents and young adults.
resources.access: Call for an appointment.
resources.caveat: Insurance, sliding-fee and service eligibility should be confirmed when scheduling.

resources.name: Care Ring Low-Cost Clinic
resources.referralTrigger: An uninsured or underinsured adult needs affordable primary care.
resources.eligibility: Adults meeting the clinic's service and financial criteria.
resources.provides: Low-cost primary care, chronic-disease management and care coordination.
resources.access: Call for eligibility and an appointment.
resources.caveat: Not an emergency clinic; appointment availability varies.

resources.name: Charlotte Community Health Clinic
resources.referralTrigger: An uninsured, underinsured or Medicaid-covered person needs primary, dental or behavioral care.
resources.eligibility: Open to community patients; discount eligibility is based on income and household size.
resources.provides: Primary care, dental, behavioral health and pharmacy-related support.
resources.access: Call for a new-patient appointment and ask about the discount program.
resources.caveat: Appointment availability and service mix differ by location.

resources.name: C.W. Williams Community Health Center
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs affordable primary care through a federally qualified health center.
resources.eligibility: Community patients; sliding-fee eligibility depends on income and documentation.
resources.provides: Primary care and related health services regardless of ability to pay.
resources.access: Call to establish care and ask about sliding-fee documentation.
resources.caveat: Bring income/insurance information; specialty access may require referral.

resources.name: Camino Health Center
resources.referralTrigger: A Spanish-speaking or immigrant young adult needs culturally responsive primary care, behavioral health, wellness or food support.
resources.eligibility: Community patients, especially uninsured/underinsured Latino families; program-specific criteria apply.
resources.provides: Bilingual primary care, behavioral health, wellness education and food pantry support.
resources.access: Contact Camino and request the appropriate service.
resources.caveat: Some services may be limited to established health-center patients.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Free and Low-Cost Clinic Directory
resources.referralTrigger: FARM127 needs to compare multiple safety-net clinics by location and service.
resources.eligibility: Eligibility varies by clinic.
resources.provides: County list of free and low-cost medical, dental and specialty-care providers.
resources.access: Use the directory, then call the selected clinic to verify intake.
resources.caveat: Directory listings do not guarantee a provider is accepting new patients.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Public Health — HIV/STI Testing and Treatment
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs confidential HIV/STI testing, treatment or prevention counseling.
resources.eligibility: Community members; service costs and appointment rules depend on test/treatment needs.
resources.provides: HIV/STI testing, treatment, education and referral.
resources.access: Call 704-432-TEST for testing help or 704-336-6500 for clinic appointments.
resources.location: Mecklenburg County public-health clinics and community sites.
resources.caveat: Walk-in and appointment procedures can change; call for current instructions.

resources.name: RAO Community Health — HIV/STI Services
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs free rapid HIV, hepatitis C or syphilis testing, PrEP or HIV-related care.
resources.eligibility: Community members; some free services are limited to Mecklenburg residents.
resources.provides: Testing, treatment linkage, PrEP and HIV supportive services.
resources.access: Call or schedule through RAO Community Health.
resources.caveat: Clinic schedules and free-service eligibility vary.

resources.name: Planned Parenthood — Charlotte Health Center
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs reproductive health care, contraception, pregnancy testing or STI services.
resources.eligibility: Patients seeking covered services; fees and consent rules depend on service and age.
resources.provides: Sexual and reproductive health services, including STI testing and treatment.
resources.access: Call or book through the Charlotte Health Center.
resources.caveat: Services, costs and insurance participation should be confirmed before the visit.

resources.name: Care Ring Nurse-Family Partnership
resources.referralTrigger: A first-time parent with limited resources needs home-visiting support during pregnancy and early childhood.
resources.eligibility: First-time mothers meeting pregnancy timing, income and service-area criteria.
resources.provides: Nurse home visits, prenatal/parenting education, health support and connection to resources.
resources.access: Call or text for eligibility screening.
resources.caveat: Enrollment must occur during pregnancy and capacity may be limited.

resources.name: NAMI Charlotte
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult or supporter needs mental-health education, peer/family support or crisis-resource guidance.
resources.eligibility: Programs vary; many are free and open to people affected by mental illness.
resources.provides: Support groups, education, advocacy and crisis-resource information.
resources.access: Use the website to find a current group or program.
resources.caveat: NAMI is not a crisis-response or clinical-treatment provider.

resources.name: Anuvia Prevention & Recovery Center
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs substance-use assessment, detox, outpatient or residential treatment.
resources.eligibility: Adolescents and adults; clinical, payer and program criteria apply.
resources.provides: Prevention, assessment, detoxification, residential and outpatient substance-use treatment.
resources.access: Call the main line for assessment; use the detox line for withdrawal-management intake.
resources.caveat: Level of care is determined clinically; bed availability and payment coverage vary.

resources.name: McLeod Centers for Wellbeing
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs evidence-based substance-use treatment, including outpatient or medication-assisted care.
resources.eligibility: Adolescents/adults depending on program; clinical and payer criteria apply.
resources.provides: Substance-use assessment and treatment across multiple levels of care.
resources.access: Call for screening and the appropriate Charlotte-area program.
resources.caveat: Program openings, insurance and medication-treatment criteria vary.

resources.name: Time Out Youth — Counseling and Support
resources.referralTrigger: An LGBTQ+ youth or young adult needs affirming counseling, groups, case support or community.
resources.eligibility: LGBTQ+ youth and young adults; age range varies by service, generally through age 24.
resources.provides: Free/low-cost counseling, support groups, case management, community and practical services.
resources.access: Contact Time Out Youth for intake and the current service calendar.
resources.caveat: Not every service is available to every age; housing and therapy may have separate waitlists.

resources.name: NCWorks NextGen — Charlotte Works
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs career coaching, paid work experience, training or help overcoming barriers to employment.
resources.eligibility: Generally ages 16–24 with one or more employment/education barriers; program eligibility applies.
resources.provides: No-cost career planning, training, credentials, supportive services and work-based learning.
resources.access: Complete a NextGen interest/intake form through Charlotte Works or Central Piedmont.
resources.caveat: Eligibility and funding-supported services require documentation; enrollment is not instant.

resources.name: NCWorks Career Centers — Charlotte Works
resources.referralTrigger: Any job seeker needs resume help, job-search support, workshops or connection to employers.
resources.eligibility: Job seekers; some funded training programs have additional eligibility.
resources.provides: Free career-center services, computers, workshops, job matching and training navigation.
resources.access: Visit or contact a local NCWorks Career Center.
resources.caveat: Training funds and program slots are limited; general career services remain free.

resources.name: Central Piedmont — Finish High School (GED/HiSET)
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs a high-school equivalency credential.
resources.eligibility: Adults and eligible minors under program rules; placement/orientation requirements apply.
resources.provides: Free preparation classes for GED or HiSET and adult high-school options.
resources.access: Complete the Central Piedmont orientation/enrollment steps.
resources.caveat: Testing fees and class schedules may vary even when instruction is free.

resources.name: Central Piedmont — College and Career Readiness
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs foundational academic, English-language, adult high-school or transition-to-college support.
resources.eligibility: Program-specific eligibility and placement requirements.
resources.provides: Adult education, English-language learning, high-school completion and career/college transition.
resources.access: Follow Central Piedmont's CCR enrollment process.
resources.caveat: Course locations, formats and start dates vary.

resources.name: Goodwill Industries of the Southern Piedmont — Charlotte Career Center
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs hands-on job search help, computer access, training enrollment or career coaching.
resources.eligibility: Open career-center services; individual training programs have separate criteria.
resources.provides: Resume/job-search help, computers, career coaching and access to skills training.
resources.access: Visit the Charlotte Career Center or review the training calendar.
resources.caveat: Course demand and enrollment windows vary.

resources.name: Urban League of Central Carolinas
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult wants no-cost occupational training and job placement support.
resources.eligibility: Program-specific age, education and income criteria may apply.
resources.provides: Training pathways including skilled trades, technology, customer service and healthcare-related programs.
resources.access: Contact the Urban League and request current program enrollment information.
resources.caveat: Course offerings, prerequisites and cohorts change.

resources.name: Road to Hire
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult wants paid training, mentorship and a pathway into a technical or professional career.
resources.eligibility: Young adults meeting the current cohort's age, education and employment criteria.
resources.provides: Paid training, professional development, mentorship and employer connections/apprenticeships.
resources.access: Review current programs and apply during an open cohort.
resources.caveat: Cohort eligibility and recruiting periods change; verify the current program before referring.

resources.name: Year Up United — Charlotte
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult wants structured job training, internship experience and employer access.
resources.eligibility: Young adults meeting the Charlotte program's current age, education and work-authorization criteria.
resources.provides: Career training, coaching, internship and job-placement support.
resources.access: Attend an information session and complete the application.
resources.caveat: Cohorts are competitive and time-bound; confirm current age and enrollment criteria.

resources.name: Mecklenburg County — More Than a Job NC
resources.referralTrigger: FARM127 needs a county-curated list of free job-driven training providers.
resources.eligibility: Eligibility varies by partner program.
resources.provides: Connections to free workforce training through partners such as Goodwill and Urban League.
resources.access: Review the listed partners and apply with the relevant training provider.
resources.caveat: This is a referral page, not a separate guaranteed-benefit program.

resources.name: NC Employment and Independence for People with Disabilities (Vocational Rehabilitation)
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult with a disability needs help preparing for, obtaining or keeping employment.
resources.eligibility: A physical, mental, intellectual or sensory disability that creates a substantial barrier to employment; formal eligibility assessment required.
resources.provides: Vocational counseling, training, job placement, assistive support and independent-living services.
resources.access: Request services through the state EIPD office.
resources.caveat: Eligibility and an individualized employment plan are required; services are not general cash assistance.

resources.name: Charlotte Mecklenburg Library — College & Career Prep
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs free online learning, resume tools, test preparation or library-based career resources.
resources.eligibility: Library card/access requirements apply to some digital tools.
resources.provides: Career, college, test-prep, technology and learning resources.
resources.access: Use the Digital Branch or ask a library staff member for help.
resources.caveat: Not a case-management or placement program; resource availability depends on library subscriptions.

resources.name: Dress for Success Charlotte
resources.referralTrigger: A low-income woman needs interview clothing, a work wardrobe and job-readiness support.
resources.eligibility: Women referred through partner agencies or meeting current intake rules.
resources.provides: Interview/employment styling, career coaching, financial education and professional development.
resources.access: Request referral/intake instructions before visiting.
resources.caveat: Services are designed for women and often require a referral appointment.

resources.name: UNC Charlotte Niner Needs
resources.referralTrigger: A currently enrolled UNC Charlotte student needs food, housing, transportation, technology, legal or emergency support.
resources.eligibility: Current UNC Charlotte students; each support has its own criteria.
resources.provides: Campus basic-needs navigation and emergency-support resources.
resources.access: Use the Niner Needs site and contact the relevant campus office.
resources.caveat: Only useful for enrolled students; emergency funds and services are limited.

resources.name: CATS Fares and Passes
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs to compare daily fares, passes and transit payment options.
resources.eligibility: Public transit riders.
resources.provides: Bus and light-rail fare information, passes and payment guidance.
resources.access: Use the official fare page and the current CATS payment method.
resources.caveat: Fares and pass products can change; verify before budgeting.

resources.name: CATS Reduced Fare Transit IDs
resources.referralTrigger: A rider with a qualifying disability, Medicare status or student category may be eligible for reduced fares.
resources.eligibility: Qualifying riders under current CATS rules; documentation required.
resources.provides: Reduced-fare identification and discounted transit fares.
resources.access: Review documentation and apply for the appropriate Transit ID.
resources.caveat: Not all low-income adults qualify; approval is category-based.

resources.name: Mecklenburg Transportation System (MTS)
resources.referralTrigger: An eligible resident needs non-emergency medical or human-services transportation.
resources.eligibility: Medicaid beneficiaries and other qualifying residents based on age, disability or program status.
resources.provides: Scheduled non-emergency medical and eligible general transportation.
resources.access: Call for eligibility and trip scheduling; Medicaid members may also need health-plan authorization.
resources.caveat: Advance scheduling and eligibility verification are required; not an on-demand ride service.

resources.name: Charlotte Center for Legal Advocacy
resources.referralTrigger: A low-income young adult needs civil legal help involving benefits, housing, health care, immigration, taxes or expunction.
resources.eligibility: Low-income residents and issue-specific service criteria.
resources.provides: Free civil legal advocacy, advice and representation in selected matters.
resources.access: Call the intake line or use Get Help; Spanish intake is available.
resources.caveat: The organization cannot accept every case; legal deadlines continue while intake is pending.

resources.name: Legal Aid of North Carolina
resources.referralTrigger: A low-income young adult needs help with eviction, domestic violence, consumer issues, benefits or another civil legal problem.
resources.eligibility: Low-income North Carolina residents; issue and conflict screening apply.
resources.provides: Free civil legal information, advice and representation in eligible cases.
resources.access: Apply online or call the statewide helpline.
resources.caveat: High demand means not every eligible applicant receives representation.

resources.name: Mecklenburg County Office of Vital Records
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult needs a Mecklenburg birth or death certificate for identification, benefits, school or employment.
resources.eligibility: Eligible applicants under state vital-record rules; identification and fees apply.
resources.provides: Certified vital records.
resources.access: Order online, by mail or in person using the county's instructions.
resources.caveat: Only records in the office's jurisdiction are available; fees and ID requirements apply.

resources.name: Safe Alliance — Victim Assistance and Sexual Assault Services
resources.referralTrigger: A survivor needs crisis counseling, court advocacy, sexual-assault support or help navigating protective options.
resources.eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault or related victimization.
resources.provides: 24/7 hotline, hospital accompaniment, counseling, court advocacy and safety planning.
resources.access: Call the Greater Charlotte Hope Line.
resources.caveat: Call 911 for immediate danger; legal representation may require referral to a legal-services provider.

resources.name: Mecklenburg County Re-Entry Services
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult recently released from incarceration needs employment, education, identification or service coordination.
resources.eligibility: Generally Mecklenburg residents within one year of release; confirm current criteria.
resources.provides: Re-entry case management, employment preparation, education and community-service connections.
resources.access: Call the Re-Entry Services office for screening.
resources.caveat: Eligibility is tied to justice involvement and release timing.

resources.name: Center for Community Transitions
resources.referralTrigger: A person affected by incarceration needs re-entry employment, family support or transition services.
resources.eligibility: People with current/former justice-system involvement and their families; program criteria vary.
resources.provides: Employment readiness, re-entry support and family-focused programs.
resources.access: Contact the organization for the appropriate program intake.
resources.caveat: Programs serve specific justice-involved populations; verify fit before referral.

resources.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult may be experiencing labor or sex trafficking, exploitation or coercive control.
resources.eligibility: Anyone seeking help or reporting a concern.
resources.provides: 24/7 confidential safety planning, crisis support and connection to local services.
resources.access: Call, text or use online chat; call 911 for immediate danger.
resources.caveat: Hotline staff coordinate options but cannot guarantee immediate housing or law-enforcement response.

resources.name: Hope for Justice — North Carolina Regional Center
resources.referralTrigger: A trafficking survivor needs trauma-informed case management and longer-term support.
resources.eligibility: Survivors meeting program criteria; confirm geographic and program eligibility.
resources.provides: Trauma-informed advocacy, case management and connection to housing, health and legal resources.
resources.access: Contact the North Carolina regional program for screening.
resources.caveat: Capacity and referral criteria vary; this is not a 24/7 emergency hotline.

resources.name: Smart Start of Mecklenburg County
resources.referralTrigger: A parenting young adult needs early-childhood, parenting or child-development resources.
resources.eligibility: Families and caregivers of young children; program eligibility varies.
resources.provides: Parent education, early-childhood navigation and connections to family supports.
resources.access: Use the families/caregivers resource page or contact Smart Start.
resources.caveat: Smart Start coordinates and funds multiple programs; availability depends on the specific partner.

resources.name: Disability Rights & Resources
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult with a disability needs independent-living skills, advocacy, benefits navigation or accessibility support.
resources.eligibility: People with disabilities; specific services may have geographic or program criteria.
resources.provides: Independent-living skills, advocacy, transportation guidance, budgeting and employment-related support.
resources.access: Contact the Center for Independent Living and request an intake.
resources.caveat: This is an independent-living and advocacy organization, not residential care or emergency assistance.

triage.situation: Immediate danger, overdose, violence or serious injury
triage.backup: Use Safe Alliance, trafficking or crisis resources after immediate safety is addressed.
triage.limit: Do not use a routine referral process for an active emergency.

triage.situation: Suicidal thoughts or acute mental-health crisis
triage.limit: Call 911 when there is immediate danger or a medical emergency.

triage.situation: Homeless tonight or unsafe place to sleep
triage.backup: Ages 16–24: The Relatives On Ramp; men: Roof Above; women/children: Center of Hope.
triage.limit: Beds and housing are limited; assessment does not guarantee placement.

triage.backup: Ask about VPA, GEAR Up, Medicaid and foster-specific education funds.
triage.limit: Many benefits end at 21; act quickly.

triage.backup: Use NC 211 and Mecklenburg Community Resource Centers for additional benefits.
triage.limit: Call before traveling; hours and capacity change.

triage.backup: Call 911 for immediate danger; Legal Aid/Charlotte Legal Advocacy for civil legal help.
triage.limit: Protect confidential location and contact information.

triage.situation: No food or basic household items
triage.firstAction: Apply for SNAP and contact Nourish Up
triage.backup: Crisis Assistance Free Store; Second Harvest food locator.
triage.limit: Emergency food should be paired with a longer-term benefits plan.

triage.situation: LGBTQ+ young adult needs affirming housing/support
triage.backup: The Relatives housing and Coordinated Entry.
triage.limit: Program age ranges and housing openings vary.

fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Refer immediately and document the young adult's custody/discharge history

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Former foster youth no longer in county custody; confirm eligibility

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Must meet state criteria and complete a voluntary agreement
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Continued placement, case management and financial support
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Ask before discharge from care; do not wait until after the 18th birthday

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Mecklenburg youth aging out; pilot criteria
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Call LINKS and verify active enrollment/funding

fosterPrograms.program: Medicaid for Former Foster Care Youth
fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Former foster-care and Medicaid history rules apply
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: State former-foster status explicitly on application

fosterPrograms.ageWindow: Often under 26 for eligible former foster youth
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Confirm plan assignment and current contact information

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Aged out at 18 or adopted after 12; NC public school; at least half time
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: FAFSA + NC Reach application before enrollment

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Current/former foster youth and some adopted/guardianship youth
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Up to program limit for approved education costs
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Coordinate ETV, financial aid and LINKS

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Leaving foster care; local program criteria
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Request Charlotte-area referral and verify openings

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Mecklenburg young people; foster history not required
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Youth-centered case management and broad resource access
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Use as a central warm-handoff hub

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Homeless, at risk or fleeing violence; screening applies

Invite young adults who want peer voice and connection

fosterPrograms.eligibilityTrigger: Federal foster-youth and homelessness criteria; local partnership required
fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Time-limited housing voucher and supportive services
fosterPrograms.farm127Action: Treat as a lead until LINKS/INLIVIAN confirms local pathway

fosterPrograms.primaryValue: Help obtaining IDs and vital documents

needsMap.primaryOptions: Coordinated Entry; The Relatives Housing; Crisis Assistance Ministry
needsMap.strategy: Use Coordinated Entry for homelessness, but pursue prevention funds before eviction whenever possible.

needsMap.primaryOptions: SNAP/FNS; Nourish Up; Crisis Assistance Free Store
needsMap.backupOptions: Second Harvest; Roof Above Day Services
needsMap.strategy: Pair emergency food with a benefits application so the plan is not pantry-dependent.

needsMap.primaryOptions: NCWorks NextGen; Goodwill Career Center; Urban League
needsMap.backupOptions: Road to Hire; Year Up; Vocational Rehabilitation
needsMap.strategy: Choose one primary workforce coach to reduce duplicated plans and missed appointments.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Central Piedmont GED/CCR; NC Reach; ETV
needsMap.backupOptions: Library College & Career Prep; UNC Charlotte Niner Needs
needsMap.strategy: Foster-specific education funds have strict age/status requirements; verify before registration.

needsMap.primaryOptions: CATS fares/passes; MTS for eligible trips
needsMap.strategy: Build a route and monthly transit budget before accepting a job or school schedule.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Teen Health Connection; Care Ring; Charlotte Community Health Clinic
needsMap.backupOptions: C.W. Williams; Camino; county clinic directory
needsMap.strategy: Establish a medical home rather than relying on emergency departments.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Teen Health Connection; Alliance Health; Santé Mobile Crisis
needsMap.strategy: Use 988/911 for crisis; routine therapy access often requires insurance and waitlist planning.

needsMap.backupOptions: Alliance Health; Roof Above wellness services
needsMap.strategy: Match the level of care to a clinical assessment; do not treat a peer mentor as treatment.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Mecklenburg DCR; Community Resource Centers; NC 211
needsMap.strategy: Track application date, case number, documents requested and appeal deadlines.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Common Wealth Charlotte; Crisis Assistance coaching
needsMap.strategy: Use counseling before high-cost loans or debt-consolidation products.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Mecklenburg Vital Records; I Am Here hotline
needsMap.strategy: Start early; missing identity documents can block work, housing, benefits and school.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Charlotte Center for Legal Advocacy; Legal Aid NC
needsMap.strategy: Legal deadlines are unforgiving; make the referral as soon as notice or court papers appear.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Child Care Resources; WIC; Nurse-Family Partnership
needsMap.backupOptions: Smart Start; Crittenton; Charlotte Family Housing
needsMap.strategy: Child care subsidy and actual provider placement are separate steps.

needsMap.primaryOptions: Safe Alliance; National Human Trafficking Hotline
needsMap.strategy: Use survivor-led safety planning and protect confidential location/contact information.
Define roles clearly so the young adult has a consistent relational through-line rather than many competing helpers.

partnerships.whyStrategic: Highest-leverage youth hub for ages 16–24; housing and broad case management
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a named referral contact and two-way warm-handoff process
partnerships.referralPathway: Referral form, consent, response-time expectation, status updates

partnerships.whyStrategic: Gateway to foster-specific benefits with hard age cutoffs
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Quarterly eligibility case review for FARM127 young adults under 21
partnerships.referralPathway: Release, eligibility checklist, age-out deadline alerts

partnerships.whyStrategic: Evidence-informed intensive transition support for eligible foster youth
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify referral criteria and how LifeSet and FARM127 mentorship can coexist
partnerships.referralPathway: Referral source, duplication boundaries, case communication

partnerships.whyStrategic: Required gateway for much of the homelessness system
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Learn the assessment process and escalation path for youth
partnerships.referralPathway: Call workflow, documents, consent, callback tracking

partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Establish document checklist and a referral contact
partnerships.referralPathway: Landlord/utility documents, appointment process, outcome feedback

partnerships.whyStrategic: Age-aligned integrated medical and behavioral care through 25
partnerships.referralPathway: Consent, insurance, no-show rescheduling, crisis boundary

partnerships.whyStrategic: Safety-net primary care and first-time-parent home visiting
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify uninsured referral and fee documentation
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility documents, appointment lead times, follow-up

partnerships.whyStrategic: Benefits, housing, health and civil legal issues commonly block stability
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Request staff training on issue spotting and urgent deadlines
partnerships.referralPathway: Intake categories, emergency escalation, document transfer

partnerships.whyStrategic: Age-specific workforce services and supportive funding
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create a shared employment referral checklist
partnerships.referralPathway: Eligibility documents, assigned coach, attendance expectations

partnerships.whyStrategic: Budgeting, credit and safe financial products fit FARM127's independence goals
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Arrange recurring financial-counseling slots or workshops
partnerships.referralPathway: Consent, attendance, coaching scope, loan boundaries

partnerships.whyStrategic: Local continuum for substance-use assessment and treatment
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Define assessment and urgent detox referral steps
partnerships.referralPathway: Clinical confidentiality, transportation, payment, discharge coordination

partnerships.whyStrategic: Child care is a frequent barrier to work and school for young parents
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Create subsidy plus provider-search referral workflow
partnerships.referralPathway: Documents, waitlist, approved activity, provider placement

partnerships.whyStrategic: Affirming housing, counseling and community for LGBTQ+ young adults
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Establish a confidential specialist referral relationship
partnerships.referralPathway: Consent, privacy, housing/therapy waitlists, role boundaries

partnerships.whyStrategic: Critical safety partner for domestic violence and sexual assault
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Request trauma-informed referral and safety-planning training
partnerships.referralPathway: Confidential contact method, emergency versus non-emergency, releases

partnerships.whyStrategic: Disability can affect work, transit, benefits and independent living
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Clarify when to refer to CIL versus vocational rehabilitation
partnerships.referralPathway: Disability documentation, goals, benefits counseling, employment plan

partnerships.whyStrategic: Primary local path for GED, adult education and affordable credentials
partnerships.suggestedFirstAsk: Identify a navigator for former foster youth and FARM127 referrals
partnerships.referralPathway: Placement testing, FAFSA, NC Reach/ETV, attendance support
